judgment.rationale: The common logger creates its daily file sink before applying the configured level, while Runner has neither a user-facing off control nor a size limit.
evidence: The report identifies about 500 MB of Runner logs and asks for disablement or a size bound.
Logger::init reads the level, creates a daily sink, and only then sets the logger level.
The persisted log settings contain logLevel, but Runner logging remains unbounded by file size.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve the hard-off and Runner-scoped bounded-log design, while selecting UI placement and defaults.

fix_assessment.rationale: No linked implementation provides both a true no-file off setting and Runner-specific bounded storage.

proposed_fixes.title: Make Runner logging disableable and size-bounded
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Logger::init opens a daily file sink before applying logLevel; retention counts days rather than bounding bytes, and no Runner control exposes these policies.
plan: When resolved logLevel is off, create or use a null logger before any file sink is opened.
Add validated Runner-only maximum bytes and file-count settings, then initialize Runner with a rotating or capped sink without changing other modules' logging policy.
Expose an explicitly restart-required logging toggle and Runner cap through the existing settings persistence path, preserving unknown fields.
Add focused logger, rotation, and settings persistence tests.
verification: Set logging off, restart PowerToys, launch Runner, and confirm the Runner log is neither created nor modified.
Use a tiny test cap, generate logs, and confirm bounded count and size while diagnostics can still read files.
Verify normal non-off module logging is unchanged.

confidence.rationale: The initialization order proves the hard-off defect; cap defaults and user experience are product-policy decisions.

issue_context.summary: Runner logs can grow substantially because the logger opens a daily file sink before honoring an off level, and its retention policy does not limit size.
known_information: The reporter has about 500 MB of Runner logs.
logger.cpp creates daily_file_sink_mt before calling set_level.
The issue asks for either disablement or a size limit.
inferences: A null logger before sink creation gives a true hard-off mode.
A Runner-only cap avoids changing diagnostics for unrelated modules.
issue_context.analysis: The current logger lifecycle supplies a direct hard-off fix. Bounded Runner storage is also concrete but needs policy values and a UI decision.
initial_investigation: Read the issue and linked retention context.
Read Logger::init and current log-level mapping.

information_gaps.information: Maintainer choice of default Runner cap, retained file count, and Settings placement
information_gaps.why_needed: These choices define supportability and UX but do not change the proven hard-off mechanism.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: During design approval, select a cap and whether the restart-required control belongs in General or Diagnostics settings.

design.root_cause: Logger::init constructs the daily sink before honoring off; daily retention does not limit each file or total bytes, and Runner has no user-facing policy.
evidence: [Observed] The issue reports substantial Runner storage.
[Inferred] A Runner-only rotating sink minimizes behavior changes.

affected_files.purpose: Resolves levels and constructs shared sinks.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The file sink is opened even when configuration resolves to off.
implementation_steps.change: Return with a null logger before sink creation for off.
implementation_steps.code_block: auto level = getLogLevel(path); if (level == spdlog::level::off) { logger = spdlog::null_logger_mt(name); return; }
edge_cases: Avoid duplicate logger registration in tests.
Do not display an initialization error for intentional off.
tests: Assert off creates and locks no target file.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Runner uses a daily sink with day-count retention only.
implementation_steps.change: Add validated Runner cap settings and a Runner-specific rotating or capped initialization path.
implementation_steps.code_block: runnerMaxBytes = validOrDefault(configuredBytes); initRotating(runnerName, path, runnerMaxBytes, runnerMaxFiles);
edge_cases: Keep non-Runner daily log behavior unchanged.
tests: Write beyond a tiny cap and assert file-count and size bounds.

implementation_steps.change: Persist a restart-required toggle and Runner cap using the existing log settings file.
implementation_steps.code_block: LoggingEnabled = logLevel != "off"; set -> save logLevel and validated Runner cap.
edge_cases: Do not promise a live logger reload.
tests: Defaults, persistence, invalid cap validation, and unknown-field preservation.

verify: Build affected logger, Runner, and Settings projects with tools\build\build.cmd.
Run focused existing logger/settings tests after locating their projects.
Perform hard-off and tiny-cap manual checks.
risks: Changing Runner filenames can affect collection scripts.
alternatives: Increase daily retention only; rejected because it does not meet either requested outcome.
Apply a global cap; rejected because it changes unrelated diagnostics.

comment.body: The current logger opens its daily sink before honoring the stored off level, so a true hard-off and Runner-only size cap have a concrete design. Before implementation, please choose the default Runner maximum size and retained file count, and whether the restart-required control belongs in General or Diagnostics settings; this will keep the change scoped without altering other modules' diagnostics.
